Chapter 4: Spiritual Gifts and the Call to Discernment
You know, not every encounter with the unknown is wrapped up in dramatic visions or extraordinary moments. Sometimes, the deepest spiritual experiences sneak up on us in the most ordinary ways—a sudden insight, a gentle nudge, or just the right word at the perfect time.
As the journey unfolded, I realized something important: spiritual gifts aren’t just for a select few. They’re available to anyone who’s willing to listen and respond, no matter where you are on your path.
There was another brush with death during a season of deep spiritual searching. I found myself spending long hours in prayer and study, trying to make sense of all the visions and experiences. And during one of those quiet times, a new awareness began to grow—a kind of clarity that let me see past the surface, to really understand the heart of things.
This gift of discernment was powerful. It helped me notice the motives and struggles that people carried, and that made compassion come much more naturally. It became easier to forgive, to reach out, and to speak truth with kindness. But let’s be honest—it wasn’t always easy. Not everyone appreciated these insights, and sometimes, the weight of knowing felt heavy. The temptation to judge or just pull back was real. Still, the call was clear: serve others, don’t condemn them.
Prophecy started showing up, too. Now and then, I’d get a word or an image—maybe a warning, a promise, or even a call to action. At first, I wondered, “Is this really from God, or am I just imagining things?” But as time went on, I began to see a pattern. The words that brought peace, hope, or conviction? They weren’t just my own thoughts. They were gifts—meant to be shared.
A lot of people think spiritual gifts are rare or dramatic, but honestly, they’re woven right into everyday life. Being able to listen, encourage, or pray for someone—these are all ways the Spirit works through ordinary folks like you and me. The secret isn’t chasing after power or attention. It’s about staying open and willing to be used, however and whenever you’re needed.
All those close encounters with death? They made the need to use these gifts feel urgent. Heaven and hell weren’t just ideas anymore—they were real, personal. I felt this deep responsibility to warn others, to invite them into a relationship with God. Not out of fear or trying to control anyone, but out of love—a real desire for others to experience the same mercy and hope I’d been given.
As things moved forward, the importance of spiritual readiness became so clear. Life’s unpredictable, and none of us know how much time we’ve got. These gifts? They’re not for personal gain—they’re meant for building others up. The real call is to live with eternity in mind, using every moment and every gift for something far bigger than ourselves.
